title: Responsive Breakpoint Systems
learning_outcomes: Explain responsive breakpoint systems and connect it to at least two of its syllabus subtopics.
Apply responsive breakpoint systems in a small SCSS example and predict the resulting CSS or compiler behavior.
Inspect the output, diagnose one plausible mistake, and state a relevant limitation or best practice.

content.intro: This lesson turns **Responsive Breakpoint Systems** into a practical, inspectable step. You will connect defining breakpoint tokens with looking up breakpoint values, then check what Dart Sass emits instead of relying on the SCSS source alone.
content.why_it_matters: Values become easier to maintain when their role and lifetime are clear. Sass variables are resolved during compilation; CSS custom properties remain in emitted CSS and can change at runtime through the cascade.

content_blocks.title: The mental model
content_blocks.text: Name values by purpose, group related tokens, and provide sensible defaults only when consumers are meant to configure the system. Test valid and missing keys, incompatible units, and the actual rendered contrast or layout.

content_blocks.title: Modern Sass note
content_blocks.text: Use Dart Sass for new work. Prefer @use / @forward and namespaced sass: built-in modules. Sass compiles to CSS; browser-native CSS features still run in the browser.

content_blocks.title: Try it yourself
content_blocks.text: Create a small SCSS example that demonstrates responsive breakpoint systems. Keep the example focused on one behavior, compile it with the version used by your project, and explain which part of the output proves your understanding.

content_blocks.title: Common mistake to avoid
content_blocks.text: Do not edit generated CSS when you intend to change source behavior. Edit the SCSS entrypoint or its module, compile again, and compare the generated output.

hints: Reduce the example to one source file and one entrypoint before adding more abstractions.
Read the first compiler diagnostic and confirm you are editing the Sass source, not only generated CSS.
Compile and inspect the emitted CSS; compare exact selectors, values, and at-rules with your expectation.

common_mistakes.problem: Assuming SCSS runs directly in the browser.
common_mistakes.why: Browsers consume CSS, not Sass syntax.
common_mistakes.fix: Compile with Dart Sass and load the resulting .css file in the HTML page.

common_mistakes.problem: Trusting source readability without inspecting generated output.
common_mistakes.why: Nesting, mixins, loops, and extension can emit unexpected selectors or more CSS than intended.
common_mistakes.fix: Compile a small example and inspect the CSS output or browser computed styles.
